item.title: From “Dune” to “The Last of Us”: How Formosa Group Elevates Storytelling through Sound
item.description: How does Formosa Group power the sound behind "Anora," "Dune," "John Wick," and "The Last of Us"? COO Matt Dubin on nurturing talent, adapting post-COVID, and why California's film tax incentive matters. "Sound is a storytelling tool, not a final step." The post From “Dune” to “The Last of Us”: How Formosa Group Elevates Storytelling through Sound appeared first on Motion Picture Association.

item.title: “Shrinking” Star & Producer Jason Segel on Season 3’s Love Letter to Los Angeles
item.description: When wildfires swept through Pasadena and Altadena in January 2025, "Shrinking" lost sets, and cast and crew lost homes. But Jason Segel, the show's executive producer, co-creator, and star, was determined to keep production in the community that had welcomed the show for years. The post “Shrinking” Star & Producer Jason Segel on Season 3’s Love Letter to Los Angeles appeared first on Motion Picture Association.

item.title: “Sinners” Oscar-Nominated Sound Mixer Chris Welcker on Rigging Michael B. Jordan’s Twin Conversations
item.description: How do you record Michael B. Jordan talking to Michael B. Jordan? "Sinners'" Oscar-nominated sound mixer Chris Welcker on capturing twin conversations, capturing Miles Caton's magical juke joint performance, and filming in Louisiana. The post “Sinners” Oscar-Nominated Sound Mixer Chris Welcker on Rigging Michael B. Jordan’s Twin Conversations appeared first on Motion Picture Association.

item.title: “Ghosts” Hair and Makeup Heads on Keeping the Beloved Show’s Spirits Looking Timeless
item.description: From a Viking explorer to a Jazz Age lounge singer, a Lenape storyteller to a 19th-century aristocrat, the ghosts of CBS's "Ghosts" span a millennium of history—and it's up to makeup department head Gillian Chandler and hair department head Jean Scarabin to bring them to life (or, rather, afterlife). The post “Ghosts” Hair and Makeup Heads on Keeping the Beloved Show’s Spirits Looking Timeless appeared first on Motion Picture Association.

item.title: Sam Mendes’ Four-Film Beatles Biopic Reveals First Look at the Fab Four
item.description: Sam Mendes revealed the first images of his Beatles cast—Paul Mescal, Harris Dickinson, Joseph Quinn, and Barry Keoghan—hidden as postcards in Liverpool. Four films, four perspectives, one legendary band. The post Sam Mendes’ Four-Film Beatles Biopic Reveals First Look at the Fab Four appeared first on Motion Picture Association.

The Mike White series is heading to France, with filming set for Paris and the French Riviera. item.title: The Incomparable Catherine O’Hara Has Passed On
item.description: If Catherine O'Hara was a scene, even acting among other comedic geniuses (as she often was), you felt drawn to her. The post The Incomparable Catherine O’Hara Has Passed On appeared first on Motion Picture Association.

item.title: Oscar-Nominated “Hamnet” Co-Screenwriter Maggie O’Farrell on Adapting Her Novel with Chloé Zhao
item.description: Maggie O'Farrell on adapting her novel Hamnet with Chloé Zhao: "The first job was to reduce the 350-page book down to a 90-odd page screenplay. There's a lot of just distilling and distilling, but I learned a lot about cinematic language from Chloé." The result? 8 Oscar nominations. The post Oscar-Nominated “Hamnet” Co-Screenwriter Maggie O’Farrell on Adapting Her Novel with Chloé Zhao appeared first on Motion Picture Association.

item.title: “Michael” Trailer Reveals Jaafar Jackson’s Transformation Into the King of Pop
item.description: The first Michael trailer is here. Jaafar Jackson plays his uncle, the King of Pop, in Antoine Fuqua's biopic exploring his explosive relationship with father Joe Jackson (an unrecognizable Colman Domingo). "I told you what to think." In theaters April 24. The post “Michael” Trailer Reveals Jaafar Jackson’s Transformation Into the King of Pop appeared first on Motion Picture Association.

item.title: Writer/Director Kleber Mendonça Filho & Best Actor Nominee Wagner Moura on Their Oscar-Nominated Thriller “The Secret Agent”
item.description: The Secret Agent could make history: if it wins Best International Feature, Brazil would become the first country in 37 years to win back-to-back. Oscar nominees writer/director Kleber Mendonça Filho & star Wagner Moura on using cinema, urban legends, and stop-motion to explore democracy's fragility. The post Writer/Director Kleber Mendonça Filho & Best Actor Nominee Wagner Moura on Their Oscar-Nominated Thriller “The Secret Agent” appeared first on Motion Picture Association.
